correctness.rationale: The 2-by-2 nilpotents exponentiate exactly. Their independently averaged Gram matrix is exactly s²(1+u²/2)I and their mean is a scaled planar rotation with squared factor s²(1+u²/4). Iterated conditioning gives both all-n identities. The sole interior minimum of F(t)=2(expm1(2t))/t² follows from strict convexity of H=t-1+exp(-2t), with t*=1-exp(-2t*) and F(t*)=2/[t*(1-t*)]. All strict/neutral h and k/a cases follow, with a concrete instance checked exactly/approximately.

originality.rationale: The per-cell randomization is from Veldman–Zuazua, but the exact all-step squared-norm/mean pair and critical all-step phase diagram are not stated in the source inspected at Example 1, Assumption 1, Theorem 1 and Remark 9. Sturman–Thiffeault consider precisely related random negative-shear products, and Gog et al. demonstrate nonnormal switching instability, but the checked theorem formulations concern generalized growth bounds, pathwise rates or alternating/noisy switching, not this complete iid balanced-generator mean-square blind spot. The boundary is derived independently from a scalar exact Gram-matrix identity. Precedence remains uncertain because the second moment is within general product-moment theory.

value.rationale: The exact thresholds distinguish long-time reliability from decay of a mean trajectory for unbiased time-splitting of a dissipative system. Even when both sampled generators are individually Hurwitz, there is a genuine open interval of fixed step sizes with exploding expected squared norm; for 3.514699...<k/a<4.970535... the mean always decays. This is a relevant noncommutative stability-design boundary, not a routine one-step normalization and not a claim for general matrices.
